youtube.title: Why Soup Cans Have Ridges 🥫 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The ridges on a food can are called beads, and they make the thin steel wall much stiffer. Cans are heated to sterilise the food and sealed, and as the contents cool a partial vacuum pulls the walls inward. The rolled-in ridges act like the folds in corrugated cardboard, helping the can resist crushing and denting.
